::: {#lorenz-vis}

```{=html}
<style>
#lz-home{margin:1.5rem 0 2rem;line-height:0}
#lz-home canvas{display:block;width:100%;height:520px;background:#000;border-radius:6px;cursor:grab}
#lz-home canvas:active{cursor:grabbing}
</style>

<div id="lz-home">
<canvas id="lhc"></canvas>
</div>
<p class="figure-caption" style="margin-top: -1rem;">A solution trajectory for the <em>Lorenz System</em>; drag to rotate.</p>

<script>
(function(){

/* ── canvas setup ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   Canvas has two sizes: CSS size (how big it looks) and pixel
   buffer size (cv.width/height). On HiDPI screens these differ
   by devicePixelRatio (usually 2). We set the buffer to the
   larger size and scale the drawing context back down, so all
   our coordinates stay in CSS pixels while output is sharp.    */
const cv  = document.getElementById('lhc');
const ctx = cv.getContext('2d');
const dpr = window.devicePixelRatio || 1;

function resize(){
  const r = cv.getBoundingClientRect();
  cv.width  = r.width  * dpr;
  cv.height = r.height * dpr;
  ctx.setTransform(dpr, 0, 0, dpr, 0, 0);
}
resize();
window.addEventListener('resize', resize);

/* ── Lorenz parameters (fixed) ────────────────────────────── */
const SIGMA=10, RHO=28, BETA=8/3;
const TOTAL=40000, DT=0.0025;

/* ── RK4 integrator ───────────────────────────────────────────
   One step of fourth-order Runge-Kutta. Takes current (x,y,z),
   returns next (x,y,z) after time DT.                          */
function deriv(x,y,z){
  return{ dx:SIGMA*(y-x), dy:x*(RHO-z)-y, dz:x*y-BETA*z };
}
function rk4(x,y,z){
  const k1=deriv(x,y,z);
  const k2=deriv(x+k1.dx*DT/2, y+k1.dy*DT/2, z+k1.dz*DT/2);
  const k3=deriv(x+k2.dx*DT/2, y+k2.dy*DT/2, z+k2.dz*DT/2);
  const k4=deriv(x+k3.dx*DT,   y+k3.dy*DT,   z+k3.dz*DT);
  return{
    x:x+(k1.dx+2*k2.dx+2*k3.dx+k4.dx)*DT/6,
    y:y+(k1.dy+2*k2.dy+2*k3.dy+k4.dy)*DT/6,
    z:z+(k1.dz+2*k2.dz+2*k3.dz+k4.dz)*DT/6
  };
}

/* ── pre-compute the full attractor ──────────────────────────
   We integrate once at startup and store all TOTAL points in a
   flat Float32Array (3 numbers per point: x,y,z). This is done
   once; the animation only reads from this array, never
   re-integrates. Float32Array is faster and more memory-
   efficient than an array of objects.                          */
const pts = new Float32Array(TOTAL * 3);
let x=0.5, y=1, z=25;
for(let i=0;i<TOTAL;i++){
  pts[i*3]=x; pts[i*3+1]=y; pts[i*3+2]=z;
  const n=rk4(x,y,z); x=n.x; y=n.y; z=n.z;
}

/* ── rotation state ───────────────────────────────────────── */
let rotX=0.42, rotZ=-0.5;
let drag=false, lmx=0, lmy=0;
const ZOOM=8;

/* ── 3D → 2D projection ───────────────────────────────────────
   Rotates a point by rotX (around X axis) then rotZ (around Z
   axis), then projects orthographically onto the screen.
   The -25 offset on z centers the attractor vertically, since
   it lives near z=25 in phase space.                           */
function proj(px,py,pz){
  const r=cv.getBoundingClientRect();
  const cx=Math.cos(rotX), sx=Math.sin(rotX);
  const cz=Math.cos(rotZ), sz=Math.sin(rotZ);
  const qz=pz-25;
  const y1=py*cx-qz*sx;
  const z1=py*sx+qz*cx;
  const x2=px*cz-y1*sz;
  return{ sx:r.width/2+x2*ZOOM, sy:r.height/2-z1*ZOOM };
}

/* ── neon color gradient ──────────────────────────────────────
   A hand-picked list of neon hues cycling through the spectrum.
   neonAt(t) takes t in [0,1] and returns an interpolated color
   by finding which two adjacent hues t falls between, then
   linearly interpolating their RGB components.                  */
const NEON=[
  '#ff2d78','#ff6b2d','#ffd12d','#2dff6b',
  '#2dd4ff','#7b2dff','#ff2de8','#ff2d78'
];
function neonAt(t){
  const scaled=t*(NEON.length-1);
  const i=Math.floor(scaled), f=scaled-i;
  const c0=NEON[i], c1=NEON[Math.min(i+1,NEON.length-1)];
  function hex(c){
    return[parseInt(c.slice(1,3),16),
           parseInt(c.slice(3,5),16),
           parseInt(c.slice(5,7),16)];
  }
  const a=hex(c0), b=hex(c1);
  return`rgb(${Math.round(a[0]+(b[0]-a[0])*f)},${Math.round(a[1]+(b[1]-a[1])*f)},${Math.round(a[2]+(b[2]-a[2])*f)})`;
}

/* ── tracer setup ─────────────────────────────────────────────
   Each tracer is an object with:
     head  — index into pts[] of the current leading point
     color — its neon color, fixed for its lifetime
   Tracers are spaced evenly around the attractor so they are
   always spread out and don't bunch up.                        */
const N_TRACERS=7, TAIL=320, SPEED=8;
const tracers=[];
for(let i=0;i<N_TRACERS;i++){
  tracers.push({
    head:  Math.floor((i/N_TRACERS)*TOTAL),
    color: neonAt(i/(N_TRACERS-1))
  });
}

/* ── ghost: the full attractor outline ───────────────────────
   A very faint trace of the entire attractor drawn first each
   frame. This gives the viewer the shape as a whole even where
   no tracer is currently passing.                              */
function drawGhost(){
  ctx.beginPath();
  const p0=proj(pts[0],pts[1],pts[2]);
  ctx.moveTo(p0.sx,p0.sy);
  for(let i=1;i<TOTAL;i++){
    const p=proj(pts[i*3],pts[i*3+1],pts[i*3+2]);
    ctx.lineTo(p.sx,p.sy);
  }
  ctx.strokeStyle='rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.04)';
  ctx.lineWidth=0.6;
  ctx.stroke();
}

/* ── draw one tracer ──────────────────────────────────────────
   The tail is split into `segs` small segments. Each segment is
   drawn at increasing opacity and lineWidth as it approaches
   the head, creating a glowing comet-tail effect.
   globalAlpha controls the canvas transparency for each stroke.
   The bright dot at the head is drawn last (on top).           */
function drawTracer(t){
  const segs=80;
  const step=Math.floor(TAIL/segs);
  for(let s=0;s<segs;s++){
    const frac=s/segs;
    const i0=(t.head - TAIL + s*step + TOTAL) % TOTAL;
    const i1=(i0+step) % TOTAL;
    const p0=proj(pts[i0*3],pts[i0*3+1],pts[i0*3+2]);
    const p1=proj(pts[i1*3],pts[i1*3+1],pts[i1*3+2]);
    ctx.beginPath();
    ctx.moveTo(p0.sx,p0.sy);
    if(i1 > i0){                  // no wraparound — draw normally
      ctx.lineTo(p1.sx,p1.sy);
    }                             // wraparound — just skip this segment
    ctx.globalAlpha = Math.pow(frac,1.5)*0.95;
    ctx.strokeStyle = t.color;
    ctx.lineWidth   = 1.0+frac*1.2;
    ctx.stroke();
  }
  ctx.globalAlpha=1;
  const hp=proj(pts[t.head*3],pts[t.head*3+1],pts[t.head*3+2]);
  ctx.beginPath();
  ctx.arc(hp.sx,hp.sy,2.5,0,Math.PI*2);
  ctx.fillStyle=t.color;
  ctx.fill();
  ctx.globalAlpha=1;
}

/* ── main animation loop ──────────────────────────────────────
   requestAnimationFrame calls this ~60 times/second.
   Each frame: clear, draw ghost, draw all tracers, advance all
   tracer heads by SPEED positions, request next frame.         */
function loop(){
  const r=cv.getBoundingClientRect();
  ctx.clearRect(0,0,r.width,r.height);
  ctx.fillStyle='#000';
  ctx.fillRect(0,0,r.width,r.height);
  drawGhost();
  for(const t of tracers){
    drawTracer(t);
    t.head=(t.head+SPEED)%TOTAL;
  }
  requestAnimationFrame(loop);
}
loop();

/* ── drag-to-rotate interaction ───────────────────────────── */
cv.addEventListener('mousedown',e=>{drag=true;lmx=e.clientX;lmy=e.clientY;});
window.addEventListener('mouseup',()=>drag=false);
window.addEventListener('mousemove',e=>{
  if(!drag)return;
  rotZ+=(e.clientX-lmx)*0.007;
  rotX+=(e.clientY-lmy)*0.007;
  lmx=e.clientX; lmy=e.clientY;
});
cv.addEventListener('touchstart',e=>{
  drag=true; lmx=e.touches[0].clientX; lmy=e.touches[0].clientY;
},{passive:true});
window.addEventListener('touchend',()=>drag=false);
window.addEventListener('touchmove',e=>{
  if(!drag)return;
  e.preventDefault();
  rotZ+=(e.touches[0].clientX-lmx)*0.007;
  rotX+=(e.touches[0].clientY-lmy)*0.007;
  lmx=e.touches[0].clientX; lmy=e.touches[0].clientY;
},{passive:false});

})();
</script>
```

:::
